strongest_angle: The 2026 Super El Niño is driving record-breaking sea-surface temperatures in the Pacific, causing unprecedented king tide flooding across Southern California coastal communities.

key_facts.fact: The Bureau of Meteorology reported that average weekly sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific have reached their highest level on record.
High tides in October 2026 caused flooding in business districts in Newport Beach and along the Pacific Coast Highway in Sunset Beach.
The 2026 El Niño Pacific Ocean temperatures have surpassed the equivalent measurements recorded during the historic 1997 and 2015 events.
Scientists estimate that king tides could rise another one to two feet in Orange County coastal neighborhoods during the 2026 El Niño event.
